subject: Executive clearance request — Enterprise Retail AWS marketplace commission / term ask
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Susan Park <susan@enterpriseretail.com>, AWS Marketplace <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Executive clearance request — Enterprise Retail AWS marketplace commission / term ask

Team,

Quick context: Enterprise Retail Co (Susan Park, procurement) is finalizing a private offer in AWS Marketplace for a multi-year commitment tied to their platform migration. They want a single private offer that rolls marketplace listing + committed reserved capacity together.

Key asks from the customer:
- One-time up-front commercial discount of 35% on list pricing (applies to first-year ACV)
- Marketplace rev-share carved from our side: they want a 70/30 split (customer-friendly), routing most incentives through partner credits.
- Net60 payment terms via procurement (their standard) and a 36-month committed term.

Why this matters: ER is a strategic, marquee retail logo for our Marketplace GTM in Q4. TCV ~ $6.8M with strong evidence of platform uplift; they are willing to nominate Redwood for a co-sell play and a case study if we can align terms quickly.

Ask to leadership/deal desk:
1) Executive OK for a one-time, conditional 35% discount on year-1 (subject to the 36-month commitment and SLA guardrails).
2) Approval to proceed with an atypical rev-share adjustment to 70/30 for this listing (AWS already signaled flexibility but needs our internal sign-off).
3) Agreement to accept Net60 for this account with Finance & Legal mitigation (PO or milestone schedule).

Attachments: draft private-offer PDF + EA_Spend_Forecast for modeled cash flow.

Timing: Susan needs a signed private offer to present to her procurement committee by Friday 9/19. If we want to move forward, I need an internal decision by EOD Wed 9/17 to lock pricing and route to AWS marketplace team.

Why I’m escalating: this combination (deep discount + rev-share carveout + extended terms) deviates materially from our standard Marketplace economics and will impact commission/recognition. I want a senior sign-off so Deal Desk and Legal can finalize redlines without rework.

Proposed guardrails (suggested for approval):
- Discount conditioned on 36-month non-cancellable commitment and milestone-based invoices (to mitigate cash risk).
- Rev-share as 70/30 for first 12 months, reverts to standard 85/15 thereafter unless AWS provides marketing credits that offset our take.
- Cap the total revenue impact to Redwood’s recognized revenue schedule (finance to validate).

Please reply with Approve / Decline / Need modifications — and tag Legal (cc’d) if you need redlines. I’ll pull in Marketplace ops once we have the greenlight.

Thanks,
Sean
Principal Account Executive
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: private-offer-draft.pdf (20 pages — commercial + SOW), EA_Spend_Forecast.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Executive clearance request — Enterprise Retail AWS marketplace commission / term ask

Sean — thanks for the summary and the modeling. A few quick flags from Rev/Marketplace POV: 

- A 35% one-time discount on year-1 is large; our typical promotional band for strategic listings is 15–25%. Anything beyond that needs exec-level business justification tied to measurable upsell/expansion covenants.
- The proposed 70/30 rev-share will materially reduce our ability to fund marketplace co-marketing and partner incentives. If we agree, we should ask AWS for explicit marketing credits or a co-funding commitment in the listing.
- Net60 + 36-month term is acceptable under strict invoicing milestones. Finance will need a structured schedule (milestones + initial deposit).

If the board is comfortable with those tradeoffs, I can sign off conditionally; my ask is that we require a performance clause: after 12 months if ARR < 70% of forecast, the discount reverts and there is a reconciliation payment.

Karthik — can Deal Desk model the commission impact under both 70/30 and a staggered rev-share (70/30 first year -> 80/20 year 2 -> 85/15 year 3)? Also can you flag the sales comp implications for Sean and the AM?

Finance (Priyom) — please validate cashflow sensitivity if Net60 is permitted with the milestone schedule.

If everyone agrees in principle, I’ll escalate to Exec Sales for formal exception.

—Marissa
SVP, Global Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Executive clearance request — Enterprise Retail AWS marketplace commission / term ask

On Mon, Sep 15, 2025 at 11:04 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Karthik — can Deal Desk model the commission impact under both 70/30 and a staggered rev-share (70/30 first year -> 80/20 year 2 -> 85/15 year 3)? Also can you flag the sales comp implications for Sean and the AM?

I ran a quick model (attached pricing-models.csv) — headline:
- If we do 70/30 Y1 -> 80/20 Y2 -> 85/15 Y3, the blended take rate drops ~12 percentage points vs our standard 85/15 across three years. Absolute net revenue delta (compared to standard listing) ~ $820k over 36 months (on the $6.8M TCV).
- Sales compensation: recommend a carveout so Sean & the AM keep target comp credit on the contracted TCV (so quota attainment unaffected), with a short-term override reduction to reflect lower company take. I’ll work with People Ops to draft the comp memo.

Counterproposal we can present to the customer (to preserve economics):
1) 25% up-front discount on Y1 (instead of 35%), with an option to scale to 35% if performance milestones are met (usage, seat growth) by month 9.
2) Rev-share: 70/30 for months 0–12 but we require AWS to commit to $150k in marketplace marketing credits that are specifically earmarked to co-op demand gen.
3) Net60 is ok if they provide a 15% initial deposit at contract signature or a PO with milestone invoicing.

If you want me to push through an exec memo, I can prepare a succinct one-pager for Marissa to present.

Karthik
Sr. Director Deal Desk
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stub: pricing-models.csv (CSV — simple model for blended take rates)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Executive clearance request — Enterprise Retail AWS marketplace commission / term ask

Team — I reviewed cash flow and revenue recognition implications of the proposed terms. High level:

- With Net60 plus a 15% deposit, our near-term cash at risk is materially lower; deposit + milestone invoicing reduces working capital pressure to manageable levels.
- Using Karthik's counterproposal (25% -> performance bump to 35%), estimated recognized revenue in year 1 declines by ~$1.05M vs list price; across 36 months the P&L impact versus standard listing is ~$650k (recognition timing smoothed by milestone invoicing).
- Accounting / RevRec: Legal + Accounting will require explicit allocation between marketplace listing fees vs dedicated reserved capacity for revenue classification. That will affect gross margin and platform-hosting costs.

Recommendation: Approve conditional discount + rev-share change if the following are accepted:
1) 15% deposit at signature + milestone schedule (detailed in EA_Spend_Forecast.xlsx).
2) Performance-based clause that allows us to reconcile shortfalls at 12 months.
3) AWS marketplace to sign an MOU for marketing credits (or explicit dollar offset) prior to listing live.

I can prepare the Finance sign-off and a short memo to attach to the exec approval.

—Priyom
Head of Revenue Ops & FP&A
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: EA_Spend_Forecast.xlsx (model + milestone schedule)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Susan Park <susan@enterpriseretail.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Executive clearance request — Enterprise Retail AWS marketplace commission / term ask

Team / Susan — after reviewing the commercial and finance notes, I am prepared to approve an exception on the following conditional basis:

1) Commercial terms: Seattle team may offer a 25% up-front discount on Y1, with a documented performance trigger to increase to 35% by month 9 if usage and seat targets are met.
2) Rev-share: Accept 70/30 for months 0–12. From month 13 onward, rev-share transitions to 80/20 then 85/15 in year 3 (per Karthik's staged model).
3) Payment terms: Net60 is permitted only with a minimum 15% deposit at signature and a milestone invoicing schedule (see EA_Spend_Forecast). No Net60 with zero deposit.
4) Marketplace ops: we require AWS to provide at least $150k in marketing credits or an equivalent co-fund arrangement tied to the listing launch. Vanessa — please coordinate with Marketplace ops to secure this and document the MOU.
5) Legal & RevRec: Legal must complete redlines to the private-offer PDF and Accounting must sign off on the revenue classification before signature.

If all of the above are documented and agreed by EOD Friday 9/19, I am signing off to proceed to AWS marketplace submission and DocuSign.

Susan — appreciate your flexibility on the deposit. If you can confirm acceptance of the 15% deposit + milestone schedule, we will finalize the private offer and route it for signature.

Marissa Cole
SVP, Global Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

On Thu, Sep 18, 2025 at 15:10 Susan Park <susan@enterpriseretail.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — we can do the 15% deposit and will work with AWS on marketing support. I will confirm formally by EOD Friday.
